title: Butter Chicken
subtitle: Rich tomato butter sauce, naan-ready
description: Rich tomato butter sauce, naan-ready. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Marinate chicken
steps.instruction: Toss cubed chicken thighs with yogurt, garam masala, garlic, ginger, and salt. Rest 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).

steps.title: Sear marinated chicken
steps.instruction: Sear chicken in butter over medium-high in batches until golden — not fully cooked through. Set aside.

steps.title: Simmer the makhani sauce
steps.instruction: In the same pot, melt butter; add crushed tomatoes, cream, and remaining spices. Simmer 15 minutes until silky. Return chicken; cook 10 minutes until 165°F.

steps.title: Serve over rice
steps.instruction: Cook basmati separately. Ladle butter chicken over rice with cilantro. The sauce should coat a spoon — add cream if it breaks.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Butter Chicken with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Butter Chicken on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Rich tomato butter sauce, naan-ready. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
